goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: Client-coordinate geometry, direct-scope normalization, modifier arbitration, serialization stripping, and targeted verification are sound, but acceptance is premature. A locked, blocked, or complex-resource primary receives neither handles nor a fallback highlight, violating visible-selection requirements. Escape can fail to cancel an active marquee when focus is editable or a dialog is open, and cancellation does not suppress the later synthesized click that can overwrite restored selection. Stage gesture coverage is source-text inspection rather than behavioral proof. One coherent remediation should close these gaps before browser QA.

worker_package.objective: Remediate the marquee slice as one coherent reliability package: provide visible primary fallback feedback when transform handles are unavailable; make active marquee and precise-pointer Escape cancellation precede focus/modal guards; suppress successor clicks after every explicit cancellation; extract stage gesture classification and state transitions into a testable controller used by main.ts; and add behavioral coverage for pan precedence, thresholds, Shift no-op, commit, pointercancel/lost capture, precise drag suppression, locked-primary feedback, clean history, and serialization.

items: src/client/canvas/marquee-selection.ts uses finite viewport client rectangles, inclusive containment/intersection, and a 4 CSS-pixel Euclidean threshold, so CSS zoom, viewBox mapping, and nested transforms do not require SVG-space conversion.

src/client/canvas/editor.ts commitMarquee freezes the active scope, enumerates only direct selectable children, preserves DOM order, unions Shift selections, and prevents ancestor/descendant co-selection.
Precise accelerator pointer handling runs in capture phase, stops propagation before draggable handlers, cancels moved sequences, toggles only within scope, and replaces across scope.
Hidden and effectively transparent ancestors are filtered while zero-thickness lines and locked visible nodes remain candidates.
Selection-only editor tests prove unchanged clean SVG bytes and no history checkpoint; serialization strips data-lineage-secondary and marquee UI remains outside SVG.

evidence.finding: Only non-primary nodes receive data-lineage-secondary. The primary receives visible feedback solely when svg.js handles are enabled, but handles are skipped for locked nodes, agent-blocked state, display:none nodes, and complex-resource nodes. Such a primary can be selected with no canvas-visible indicator.
evidence.required_fix: Add an editor-only primary fallback marker and visible blue treatment whenever handles cannot be installed; remove it during deselection and strip it from all clean serialization and snapshots.

evidence.finding: Editable-focus and open-dialog guards return before active marquee cancellation. cancelMarquee and cancelPrecisePointer also release state/capture without arming click suppression, so a subsequent synthesized click can clear or toggle the restored selection.
evidence.required_fix: Handle Escape for an active marquee or precise pointer before ordinary focus/modal guards, restore the pre-gesture selection, and suppress the successor click on every explicit cancellation path.

evidence.finding: Pan-versus-marquee coverage reads main.ts and asserts source substrings. It does not execute pointer precedence, threshold transitions, commit, cancellation, lost capture, or additive below-threshold behavior.
evidence.required_fix: Move gesture classification/state transitions into a testable controller used by main.ts and replace the source-string interaction assertions with event/state behavioral tests.

acceptance_checks: A locked or otherwise handle-ineligible primary has a visible blue fallback marker; ordinary handle-enabled primary behavior remains unchanged.
Fallback primary and secondary markers are absent from clean serialization and snapshots.
Escape cancels an active marquee or precise pointer even when an input is focused or a dialog is open, and an immediate successor click cannot change restored selection.

Behavior-level tests execute middle/Space pan precedence, blank-primary marquee, object-primary non-marquee, 3px pending, 4px activation, unmodified below-threshold clear, Shift below-threshold no-op, commit, pointercancel, and lost-capture cancellation.
A precise-modifier pointerdown cannot reach a simulated object-drag listener, and moved or cancelled precise sequences neither select nor mutate.
